profilePeriod: Political career and published positions through September 2026; prime minister 2015–2018.

sources.title: States unwilling to take responsibility for increasing taxes
sources.evidence: Proposed states levy income tax to match responsibility for schools and hospitals; proposal rejected by states.

sources.title: National Security Statement
sources.evidence: Supported control orders, continued detention of high-risk convicted terrorists, restrictions on bail/parole, metadata and access to encrypted communications; defended anti-IS military operations.

sources.title: The Politics of Love, McCosker Oration
sources.evidence: Practising Catholic praises Christian love and charity; rejects Christian nationalism and ethnic/religious tests for migrants; defends pluralism, opposition rights and compromise. Reaffirms that he did not intend to sell Medicare.

sources.title: Submission to the AUKUS public inquiry
sources.evidence: Criticises AUKUS submarine dependence, reduced sovereign control and inadequate parliamentary scrutiny; calls for alternate French submarine acquisition, retaining defence capability.

sources.title: BNEF Summit New York 2026
sources.evidence: Supports renewable electrification, batteries and pumped hydro on engineering/economic grounds; cooperation between middle powers and continued US alliance; alarmed by proliferation risks.

sources.title: Historic Snowy Deal
sources.evidence: Federal acquisition of all Snowy Hydro shares, retaining public ownership and supporting pumped hydro; agreed state sale proceeds invested in infrastructure.

sources.title: Press Conference on enterprise tax plan
sources.evidence: Defends company tax reductions for investment/jobs; abandons extension to large firms after Senate rejects; retains energy supplement.

sources.title: Keynote Address to the 2017 Asia Pacific Regional Conference
sources.evidence: Defends open markets, TPP11, RCEP, EU and Peru negotiations; opposes protectionism and rival closed blocs.

sources.title: Strengthening integrity of Australian citizenship
sources.evidence: Joint PM release proposed competent English, four years permanent residence, Australian civic values; explicitly celebrates multicultural immigration.

sources.title: Putting Australian workers first
sources.evidence: Replaced 457 visa with tighter skills-shortage visas and English/criminal checks; prioritised resident workers while retaining migration.

sources.title: Turnbull talks abortion at Christian conference
sources.evidence: Catholic faith alongside abortion choice and anti-discrimination. His then opposition to gay marriage was subsequently superseded.

sources.title: Speech introducing same-sex marriage plebiscite bill
sources.evidence: Supports marriage equality while proposing popular plebiscite and protections for religious celebrants.

sources.title: Human embryo research bill second reading
sources.evidence: Turnbull supports somatic cell nuclear transfer and therapeutic research, distinguishing it from reproductive human cloning.

sources.title: Assisted dying: Victoria approves bill
sources.evidence: Turnbull opposed euthanasia, but respected Victorian jurisdiction.

sources.title: I will be voting yes to establish an Indigenous voice
sources.evidence: Supports a constitutionally enshrined advisory Indigenous Voice, not a chamber with a parliamentary veto. Reversed his government’s 2017 rejection; retains reservations about constitutionally reserved representation.

sources.title: No jab no play no pay
sources.evidence: Supports making vaccination a condition of family payments and childcare participation.

sources.title: Facial recognition is not mass surveillance: Turnbull
sources.evidence: Supports biometric identification data-sharing; said CCTV images would not be included in national database.

sources.title: Malcolm Turnbull, National Archives of Australia
sources.evidence: Independent institutional biographical record for 29th prime minister, 2015–2018.

sources.title: A Bigger Picture by Malcolm Turnbull, Hardie Grant
sources.evidence: Publisher identifies self-authored bestselling political memoir of 2020. No Brazilian translation located by dedicated Portuguese title search; retain original title.

sources.title: Media index
sources.evidence: Checked through 2026-10-01; September interviews listed, recent policy material includes August AUKUS and Catholic social-services speeches.

facts: 2016 state income-tax proposal shifts fiscal responsibility to state governments.
Respected Victorian assisted-dying legislative jurisdiction despite disagreement.
Snowy buyout centralised ownership of a national asset.
estrutura.tension: Federal autonomy is bounded by national coordination and constitutional powers, not unilateral secession.

facts: Democratic compromise and minority rights defended in 2026.
Demands parliamentary scrutiny of AUKUS.
Supports republic and advisory Indigenous Voice.
representacao.tension: Parliamentary democracy with checks, not permanent assemblies or unelected expert rule; referendums supplement institutions.

facts: 2017 expansion of surveillance/control orders/detention and encryption access.
Vaccination-linked benefits.
Biometric sharing with stated limits, and reservations about assisted dying.
poder.tension: Security-oriented liberal democrat: due process and political opposition coexist with exceptional counterterror powers; convicted-offender detention is not evidence for limitless detention of any suspect.

facts: 2017 English/civic integration and skills restrictions.
2026 explicitly rejects race, religion or nationality as tests of immigrant character.
imigracao.tension: Celebrates pluralism while rejecting unrestricted borders and demanding common civic duties; cultural difference alone is not grounds for exclusion.

facts: Military participation against IS in 2017.
2026 insists on viable submarine defence and warns of proliferation.
diplomacia.tension: Armed defence and allied cooperation coexist with skepticism about avoidable war and dependence; no pacifism or nuclear-weapons advocacy.

facts: Anti-IS intervention and training Iraqi forces.
2026 demands sovereign decision-making rather than US-directed submarine dependence.
Supports middle-power cooperation and rules-based international system.
intervencao.tension: Rejects both isolation and subordination to great-power adventurism; national interest operates within alliances and international law.

facts: Company tax reductions for private investment.
Federal public ownership of Snowy explicitly guaranteed.
Rejects privatising Medicare.
economia.tension: Private enterprise with public healthcare, safety net and selected strategic infrastructure, not socialist ownership or privatisation of everything.

facts: Tax competitiveness and private investment.
State-supported infrastructure, energy transition and retained energy supplement.
controle.tension: Market-led growth accepts regulation, central banking, safety nets and coordination where infrastructure or externalities require it.

facts: TPP11 and wider trade liberalisation explicitly promoted.
2017 skilled migration restricted to shortages.
2026 energy independence via renewables.
comercio.tension: Strong free-trade outlook does not mean abandoning critical resilience, national-interest investment review or defence procurement.

facts: 2026 Catholic worship, Gospel and charity explicitly inform his moral language.
Rejects Christian nationalism.
Supports abortion choice and marriage equality against conservative doctrine.
religiao.tension: Personally religious and positive toward faith communities while upholding plural civil law; neither theocrat nor militant atheist.

facts: Abortion choice defended in 2008.
Later marriage-equality support supersedes his 2008 opposition.
Supports Indigenous Voice and opposes ethnic/religious prejudice.
moral.tension: Social liberalism coexists with valuing family and reservations about euthanasia; no verified radical position on all contemporary identity questions. His marriage-equality argument values durable family commitment, not a rejection of family institutions.

facts: 2006 therapeutic embryo research support within limits on reproductive cloning.
2026 renewables, batteries and pumped hydro development.
2026 warns digital algorithms can deepen social division.
tecnologia.tension: Technological optimism is bounded by environmental protection and biomedical ethics; not unlimited transhumanism.

limitations: Simulation of 240 responses, not claims of verbatim answers. Brazil-specific items are interpreted by their institutional/policy equivalents.

Direct evidence is weaker on cryptocurrency, brain implants, cultured meat, polyamory and detailed racial quota design; cautious directional inferences are identified rather than treating silence as neutrality.
Later explicit positions supersede older positions; prior government actions remain relevant where no renunciation found. Latest-source check performed 2026-10-01.
Portuguese book search did not establish a Brazilian translated edition. Publisher page opened successfully once, then a later request encountered a redirect limit.

recommendedMetadata.status: current PT/EN accurate; no correction needed

bookDecision.reason: Self-authored political memoir; publisher calls it a bestselling political memoir of 2020. No existing entry was found; original title retained without verified Brazilian translation.

processNotes: Read all controlling documents and saved prompt before research; consulted only metadata and existing research period/source URLs, no stored answers, vectors or score reports.

Likely neighbours before answering: Tony Abbott and Scott Morrison share Liberal Party markets/security but differ from Turnbull on republic, climate policy and marriage equality; Anthony Albanese shares marriage equality and climate action but comes from Labor with stronger union/public-sector commitments. No numerical targets or other profile answers consulted.
One independent audit only. Original validation will be run once after answers, with any warnings/blockers reported without score tuning.

Metadata was confirmed accurate to coordinator before answers; research and updated prompt were written before generating answers. All 240 questions remain verbatim and fresh archetype block appended.

Answers selected individually in shuffled question order. No answer changes after validation; observed duplicate blocker retained for coordinator/user decision. Validation was repeated only to capture process exit status with full output.
